sources.title: Joyce Burnette, review essay on Ivy Pinchbeck, Women Workers and the Industrial Revolution, EH.net
sources.citation: Joyce Burnette, “A Pioneer in Women’s History: Ivy Pinchbeck’s Women Workers and the Industrial Revolution, 1750–1850,” EH.net, Economic History Association, original displayed review essay; original posting date not established from current page.

verification.note: Complete original displayed review essay and reference list freshly read via successful web-tool rendering; local HTTP403 supplied no body and is not counted as reading. Distinguishes corroboration of employment patterns from dispute over welfare interpretation; critiques wage theory while praising source range and later usefulness. Davidoff/Hall comparison is joint, class-specific and mediated. Quoted original studies remain unread; historical citation-count and life assertions not independently adopted. Current migration/copyright date is not original review date.

pinchbeck.note: Fresh licensed publisher preview actual PDF reading: copyright and edition statement, full 1969 reprint preface signed October 1968, full original 1930 preface vi visually collated on PDF leaf 7, complete introduction 1–5, opening agriculture 7 and selected 10–11 and 22 with their notes. Remainder of occupational chapters and conclusion 306 onward unread. Distinctions among class, marital position, family work and paid employment remain; optimistic net benefit is Pinchbeck’s interpretation. New selected 10–11 shows skilled dairy responsibility, 22 common rights resources, while historical witnesses and Hammond mediation are not fresh original readings. Knowles and Power’s distinct guidance and Mrs Bernard Shaw’s scholarship retained.
